children: Stock index futures were lower before the bell Tuesday as continued selling in Nvidia (
) and other AI-linked stocks weighed on market sentiment ahead of the chipmaker's results.
Now, here are four news stories that broke overnight to watch out for:
Nvidia board rejects Jensen Huang return:

bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, despite a growing campaign for his return following his resignation over affairs involving employees and suspected Chinese intelligence ties. More than 180,200 people have signed a petition demanding Huang's reinstatement, with backing from Elon Musk and President Donald Trump. Taiwan's Taipei 101 skyscraper was illuminated Monday with messages including "Taiwan Loves Jensen," and prominent shareholders such as Atreides Management's Gavin Baker and Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner have urged the company not to rush a replacement.

a significant rebalancing of its equity holdings in the third quarter. The chipmaker raised its SpaceX stake to 130.5 million shares from 122.8 million at the end of June, while cutting its Intel position by 25% to 161.1 million shares from 214.8 million. The shift puts SpaceX ahead of Intel as Nvidia's largest disclosed equity investment, with the SpaceX stake valued at approximately $19.7 billion versus $19.4 billion for Intel. The two investments now account for more than 80% of Nvidia's $48.3 billion disclosed portfolio, which shrank from $63.4 billion in Q2.
Visa and Mastercard push $38 billion settlement:

a federal judge in Brooklyn to approve their proposed $38 billion settlement with merchants over credit card swipe fees, as the agreement faces more than 1,000 objections from businesses including Walmart, Circle K, and the National Retail Federation. U.S. District Judge Brian Cogan did not issue a ruling at Monday's hearing but indicated that rejection could send the 21-year-old antitrust dispute to trial. The proposed settlement covers more than 12 million merchants and would reduce interchange fees by 0.1 percentage point over five years while capping fees on standard consumer credit cards at 1.25% for eight years.
Situational Awareness hedge fund rebuilt AI stakes before October slump:

Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness hedge fund  rebuilt its AI stock portfolio in the third quarter, taking major stakes in SharonAI, CleanSpark, IREN, Bitdeer Technologies, and Fermi just before sharp losses across its holdings. The CleanSpark stake is worth almost $39 million, while IREN and Bitdeer stakes exceed $21 million and $20 million, respectively. The fund also held call options in Nebius, Sandisk, the Roundhill Memory ETF, and Bloom Energy at the end of September. SharonAI posted a 55% loss in October, IREN fell 41%, and Nebius declined 35%.
